Sept. 18th, 37.

Report on posters found pasted in Central District bearing oaths and slogans for the Chinese people in connection with the Mukden Incident of September 18, 1931.

Det.Insp. A. Telfer

Sir,

During the morning of September 18, 1937 posters were found pasted up in Central District bearing the following oaths and slogans:-

The oaths for Chinese People pledging support to the National Government.

1. I hereby make a resolute oath as follows:-
a. Up with the National Government.
b. Obey the leader.
c. Sacrifice for the war of defense to the end.

2. Defend Shanghai by force of arms.

3. After a steady fight, the final victory will belong to us.

4. Down with the Imperialism of Japan prior to seeking world's peace.

5. Cooperate with other races who are seeking peace in the world in attacking the Japan Imperialism.

6. Fight it out to the end.

7. Energy from those who have strength and money from the wealthy. Use our blood and flesh for freedom.

8. Offer a mass resistance to the end.

9. Fight for the race's existence.

10. It is glorious to sacrifice for the country.

11. Down with the notorious Japan Imperialism.

12. It is the only way, fight it out against the Japan Imperialism.

13. Long live the Chinese Republic. Exterminate the Chinese traitors.

14. Remember Sept. 18th anniversary by action.

〔此处转录不清：左侧有多处手写签名及“DEPUTY COMMISSIONER”印章〕

Political                                September 17, 1937.

Anniversary of the Mukden Incident - observance

In commemoration of the 6th anniversary of the Mukden
Incident, the local Tangpu situated at Feng Ling Jao, off
Route Ghisi, has published in the newspapers the following
measures for observance by the local populace on September 18:

1. That the national flag be hoisted at half mast.

2. That all the people should eat a vegetarian diet on that
day and donate the money thus saved towards the fund for
comforts to the troops.

3. That "Kwang" cakes instead of "moon" cakes be eaten on
that day.

4. That all residents should observe a three minute silence
at noon, after which they should raise their right hands
and take oaths pledging support to the National Government
in resisting the enemy.

Members of the Cultural Circles Race Salvation
Association will also cooperate with local public bodies
in conducting propaganda on this occasion between 9 a.m.
and 5 p.m. September 18. This movement will be in the form
of (a) open-air performance, (b) open-air lectures, (c)
theatrical performance, and (d) distribution and posting of
pictorials and handbills. The places where these activities
will be carried out are (1) alleyways, (2) refugee camps,
and (3) wounded soldiers hospitals. throughout Shanghai.

The number of persons participating in this movement,
who will be organized into groups of some five persons each,
is estimated to be about 300.              〔此处转录不清〕

Miscellaneous

Refugees leave Shanghai

Approximately 1,600 refugees left Shanghai by train
for various places along the Shanghai-Hangchow-Ningpo and
Nanking-Shanghai Railways on September 16.

沈阳事变周年纪念 - 纪念活动

为纪念沈阳事变六周年，位于极司菲尔路（Route Ghisi）旁丰林角（Feng Ling Jao）的当地塘铺已在报纸上发布以下措施，供当地民众于 9 月 18 日遵守：

1. 降半旗致哀。

2. 当日全民素食，并将省下的钱捐赠给慰劳军队基金。

3. 当日吃“光”饼而非“月”饼。

4. 所有居民应在中午默哀三分钟，随后举起右手，宣誓支持国民政府抵抗敌人。

文化界救亡协会成员也将配合当地公共团体，在 9 月 18 日上午 9 时至下午 5 时期间开展宣传。此次活动形式包括 (a) 露天表演，(b) 露天演讲，(c) 戏剧演出，以及 (d) 分发和张贴画报和传单。开展这些活动的地点包括 (1) 弄堂，(2) 难民营，以及 (3) 全上海的伤兵医院。

参与此次运动的人数估计约为 300 人，将组织成每组约五人的小组。              〔此处转录不清〕

杂项

难民离开上海

9 月 16 日，约 1,600 名难民乘火车离开上海，前往沪杭甬铁路和京沪铁路沿线的各地。
